newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: US offers $14 million aid for new Congo -radio.
newsitem.headline: US offers $14 million aid for new Congo -radio.

text.p: The United States has offered $14 million to president Laurent Kabila's Congo as part of an aid package for the rehabilitation of the basic infrastructure of the vast Central African country, state radio said on Thursday.
It quoted the US ambassador Daniel Simpson in Kinshasa as saying that initially that the United States would give $3 million.
The radio did not say if it was a loan or a donation.

Speaking on state television after meeting president Kabila, Simpson said, "We are here to help. President Kabila is not a dictator. He has repeatedly expressed his willingness to hold elections in the Congo in a relatively short period of time."

Ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko ruled the country single- handedly from 1965 to 1997. He has fled into exile but has left behind him a country economically ruined, with a foreign debt estimated at $14 billion.
Kabila grabbed power in May after a seven-month military campaign. He has pledged to turn Africa's third largest country into a prosperous state.
But the government said that it had inherited empty state coffers.
